objective: The transcript segmenter discards short lines that contain a date. server/services/sources/segmenter.ts ~L291 `const bareTimestamp = TIMESTAMP_RE.test(firstLine) && text.trim().length <= 40;` and ~L298 treat any block of 40 characters or fewer containing a date as a pure timestamp marker and `continue`, so its text never reaches a segment. Reproduced: blocks 'You: when do we launch?', 'Assistant: We settled it.', 'Launch is 2026-10-01, final.', 'Anything else?' lose the launch sentence entirely and split 'Anything else?' from the assistant turn. CLAUDE.md §11: every claim about a transcript resolves to a passage in it. Fix: treat a block as a bare timestamp only when, after removing the matched timestamp, nothing remains but punctuation, AM/PM, weekday or month names; otherwise it is ordinary content that still records its timestamp on the current segment.
expectedOutcome: Dated sentences stay in their segment; genuine timestamp-only blocks are still consumed as markers.

acceptanceConditions.statement: tests/segmenterDatedLine.test.ts: the reproduction keeps 'Launch is 2026-10-01, final.' inside the Assistant segment's text.
A block that is exactly '2026-10-01' or '[10:32 AM]' is still consumed as a marker and sets timestampText on the next segment.
The existing source-ingestion tests pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the commit; affects newly ingested sources only.
